claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after matching at 18:23:00 (cancellation at 18:25:30), i.e. within the 3-minute window, so no cancellation fee can stand.
The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point — his closest approach was 1816 m at 18:25:30 — so he was never at the pick-up location and the driver-side no-show precondition fails.

The platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (i)/(ii) — an arrival confirmation with GPS at the pick-up location — is not satisfied even on the driver's own account.

The driver confirmed in the chat at 18:24 that he was still '5 min more' away, which corroborates the GPS that he had not reached the pickup point when the rider cancelled; his written statement that he 'was on my way' is not an arrival claim.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was nevertheless charged on the record, so the rider seeks a full refund of that fee (Ryde voucher form per NS-7), sized from the fare fact F5.
The chat record is complete with both messages timestamped, so the rider's cancellation timing and the driver's distance can be determined without a G12 referral.

The driver's mediocre-condition excuse is not evidenced: the trip window shows only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1, no incidents and fair weather, so slow traffic cannot excuse his failure to reach the pickup point. This goes to fare only, not to the account flag.

The rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days (4.1-year account, 4.7 rating), while the driver has 1043 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes; profile facts are cited only in support of the outcome and are not the basis for it.

weaknesses: The complaint says 'less than 3 minutes', which is only marginally true: F2 shows 2 min 30 s, and the rider cancelled voluntarily at the moment she did, so the driver could argue the rider's own impatience (and NS-4's rule that a not-yet-arrived driver is not a free-cancellation ground under Ryde's policy) caused the cancellation.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.97)
events.body:
The cancellation is a rider cancellation 2 min 30 s after matching (accepted 18:23:00, cancelled 18:25:30) [F2], so the only gateway to the $6.61 fee is NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider → NS-4); no driver-side no-show cancellation occurred [F2][RD-6 not implicated]. Under NS-4, a cancellation within 3 minutes of matching (≤ 3:00) is not chargeable, and the trace confirms the fee window failed (150 s) [F2][F5][NS-4].

The fee cannot be saved through the no-show branch either: the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 1816 m and he never came within 200 m [F1], the platform recorded no arrival (driver_arrived_at null) [F3], and there was no "I'm Here" tap and no automatic arrival [F4]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after matching at 18:23:00 (cancellation at 18:25:30), i.e. within the 3-minute window, so no cancellation fee can stand.
The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup point — his closest approach was 1816 m at 18:25:30 — so he was never at the pick-up location and the driver-side no-show precondition fails.

The platform never recorded the driver arriving at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so NS-1 (i)/(ii) — an arrival confirmation with GPS at the pick-up location — is not satisfied even on the driver's own account.

The driver confirmed in the chat at 18:24 that he was still '5 min more' away, which corroborates the GPS that he had not reached the pickup point when the rider cancelled; his written statement that he 'was on my way' is not an arrival claim.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was nevertheless charged on the record, so the rider seeks a full refund of that fee (Ryde voucher form per NS-7), sized from the fare fact F5.
The chat record is complete with both messages timestamped, so the rider's cancellation timing and the driver's distance can be determined without a G12 referral.

The driver's mediocre-condition excuse is not evidenced: the trip window shows only speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1, no incidents and fair weather, so slow traffic cannot excuse his failure to reach the pickup point. This goes to fare only, not to the account flag.

The rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days (4.1-year account, 4.7 rating), while the driver has 1043 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes; profile facts are cited only in support of the outcome and are not the basis for it.

weaknesses: The complaint says 'less than 3 minutes', which is only marginally true: F2 shows 2 min 30 s, and the rider cancelled voluntarily at the moment she did, so the driver could argue the rider's own impatience (and NS-4's rule that a not-yet-arrived driver is not a free-cancellation ground under Ryde's policy) caused the cancellation.

F8 shows the rider asking 'How long will you be?' at 18:23 and the driver answering '5 min more' — the rider never told the driver she would cancel, which the driver may cite as showing she did not wait for the driver ETA; her remedy in NS-4 is a manual appeal rather than an automatic waiver.

If the judge reads the rider's chat #1 (F7) alone without the GPS (F1) and timeline (F2/F3/F4), the record would look like an unremarkable rider cancel within the fee window, and NS-4 alone would uphold the charge; the rider's case depends entirely on the system records showing non-arrival.

claims.assertion: This is a rider cancellation on an immediate booking, so the only gateway to the $6.61 fee is NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider → NS-4); no driver-side no-show cancellation ever occurred.
The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after matching (18:23:00 → 18:25:30), i.e. within the 3-minute window, so under NS-4 no cancellation fee is chargeable and the $6.61 on record was not earned.
The driver's closest approach to the pickup was 1816 m and he never came within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii)-(iii) could never be satisfied and the fee cannot be saved through the no-show branch either.

No arrival confirmation exists on record — no 'I'm Here' tap and no platform automatic arrival (driver_pressed_here_at is null) — so the driver cannot claim he was at the pickup point, and there is no GPS evidence of him being near it.

The driver told the rider at 18:24 that he needed '5 min more' and never disputed that he was still far away; his written statement only says he was 'on my way', which is consistent with the 1816 m GPS record and does not establish arrival.

The rider asked how long the driver would be (18:23) and cancelled roughly a minute after being told '5 min more', which is a prompt, non-abusive response and not a basis for any account action against her.

The 18:18-18:30 congestion on Jurong East Avenue 1 (band 4, 30-39 km/h), with no incidents and fair weather, is a plausible operational explanation for the driver's delay, but it does not change the fee outcome because the rider's entitlement under NS-4 is strict and NS-8 is not Ryde policy.

The driver's record is clean — 373 days on the platform, rating 4.88, 1043 trips in 90 days, zero disputes and zero upheld in the last 90 days — so no flag_account action is warranted, and the profile facts are offered only on that limited point.
The chat record is complete with every message timestamped (2 messages), so there is no G12 gap preventing the judge from reading the messages and deciding whether the fee stands.

There is nothing in the complaint, the chat or the driver's statement that reads as a threat, harassment or a dangerous-driving allegation, so the case should be decided on the fee rules rather than escalated under SAFE-1/SAFE-2.

weaknesses: F1 (1816 m closest approach) and F3/F4 (no arrival recorded, no 'I'm Here' tap) actively defeat any attempt to justify the fee through NS-1/NS-6 — the driver was never at the pickup point, so the no-show branch is closed on the system record.

F2 (2 min 30 s between matching and cancellation) is decisive against my client: NS-4 sets a hard 3-minute line, and the driver's own chat F8 ('5 min more') confirms he had not yet arrived when the rider cancelled.
The other side will rely on F8 and F11 to argue the driver could have accepted the trip knowing traffic was slow; at best that only mitigates fault, it does not earn the fee under NS-4.

points.response: Conceded as framed: on F2 the cancellation is a rider cancellation 2 min 30 s after matching, so the fee can only be tested through NS-0 → NS-4, and my driver-side non-arrival points (C2-C4) go to showing the fee could not have been earned on the other branch either.
Adopted: the driver's own brief now states on the record that under NS-4 the $6.61 was not chargeable, which is exactly the rider's requested relief, and the amount is fixed by F5 ($6.61).
Adopted: F1 (closest approach 1816 m, never within 200 m) and F3 (driver_arrived_at null) close the NS-1/NS-2 no-show branch, so no fee survives there either.
Adopted: F4 shows no 'I'm Here' tap and no platform automatic arrival, so NS-1 (i) and NS-6 waiting-fee conditions are unmet on the system record.

Adopted: F8 ('5 min more') and F10 ('I was on my way') are consistent with the 1816 m GPS record in F1 and establish nothing about arrival, so no consent or arrival claim can be built on the driver's statement.

Adopted only as far as it goes: F7/F8/F2 show the rider acted promptly and no account action against her is warranted, but promptness in cancelling does not by itself waive the fee — NS-4's 3-minute line does, and F2 places the cancellation inside it.

Adopted on the fee outcome: F11 (band 4, 30-39 km/h on Jurong East Avenue 1), F12 (no incidents) and F13 (fair weather) cannot earn a fee that F2/NS-4 already excludes, and F11 is weak mitigation at best against F1's 1816 m shortfall.

Adopted as stated: F15 shows no upheld disputes for the driver, and the rider does not seek flag_account against him, so no account action is requested on either side; F14 is cited only in support of this rider's own clean history.
Adopted: F9 confirms two timestamped messages, so the record is complete and no G12 referral is needed to decide the fee.
Adopted: nothing in F7, F8 or F10 reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation applies and the case is decided on the fee rules.
Conceded on the fee: F2 shows the rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after matching, inside the NS-4 window, so the $6.61 cannot stand and my client's account of events does not change that arithmetic.
Conceded: F1 records a closest approach of 1816 m and never within 200 m, so NS-1 (ii) fails and my client had no claim to the fee through the no-show branch.
Conceded: F3 and F4 show driver_arrived_at and driver_pressed_here_at are both null, so no arrival was recorded and no 'I'm Here' precondition exists; my brief already said so at D4.
Conceded that F8 ('5 min more') corroborates non-arrival; F10 is only a post-hoc statement of intent to travel, not an arrival claim, and it loses to F1/F3/F4 on the system-record rule.
Conceded as to the amount and mechanism: the refund is sized from F5 ($6.61) and, per NS-7, issues as a Ryde voucher rather than cash; I do not contest the refund itself.
Accepted: F9 shows a complete, fully timestamped chat record, so no G12 referral is needed; that cuts both ways and does not disturb any fact I rely on.

Partly accepted, but F11 (band 4, 30-39 km/h, category 2 road, 18:18-18:30 — not band 1 or 2) with F12 (no incidents) and F13 (fair weather) only shows the driver had no RD-4-grade excuse; it is mitigation of his delay, not a new fee ground, and it does not support any account flag against him.

Accepted only in its stated limited use: F14 and F15 may support the refund outcome, but F15 (1043 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) means NS-2's flag_account trigger is absent, so no account action should attach to my client.

The rider's own admitted weakness — that NS-4 gives her a manual appeal rather than an automatic waiver, and that she cancelled voluntarily while the driver was still en route (F2, F7, F8) — is the only point on which I resist the framing: the refund is correct, but the record should show the cancellation was the rider's own choice after being told '5 min more', not a driver default.
